subject: Vocabulary
description: High-hit antonym pairs from SSC/banking PYQ; common confusion clusters

options.option_text: Crystal-clear, openly visible
Opaque, blocking all light through
Translucent, partially see-through
Open, exposed and unhidden

questions.explanation: TRANSPARENT = clear; allows light to pass; honest, open. ANTONYM = OPAQUE = blocking light, not see-through; (figurative) hard to understand, hidden. Translucent (partially see-through, e.g., frosted glass) is BETWEEN transparent + opaque. Common figurative use: 'transparent governance' vs 'opaque dealings'. SSC PYQ word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Concise, with brief expression
Verbose, using too many words
Reserved, holding back speech
Dramatic, with theatrical effect

questions.explanation: LACONIC = using few words; concise to the point of curtness. (From SPARTANS — natives of Laconia, Greece — famously brief in speech. When Philip II of Macedon threatened 'If I invade Lakonia, I will raze your city', Spartans replied just 'IF'.) ANTONYM = VERBOSE = wordy, long-winded. Other antonyms: garrulous, loquacious, prolix. Synonyms of laconic: terse, brief, succinct, pithy, curt.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Brief, lasting a short while
Permanent, lasting for very long time
Sudden, happening unexpectedly fast
Visible, openly seen by all

questions.explanation: EPHEMERAL (Greek 'ephemeros' = lasting one day) = short-lived, fleeting, transient. 'Ephemeral fame', 'ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms'. ANTONYM = PERMANENT, eternal, enduring, perpetual, everlasting. Synonyms of ephemeral: fleeting, transient, transitory, momentary, evanescent, short-lived. Common SSC PYQ word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Sociable, enjoying company very much
Solitary, preferring to be alone
Friendly, kind to other people
Lively, full of energy always

questions.explanation: GREGARIOUS (Latin 'grex' = flock) = fond of company, sociable; (zoology) living in flocks/herds. People who enjoy social gatherings + lots of friends are gregarious. ANTONYM = SOLITARY, reclusive, antisocial, introverted, withdrawn. Note: 'gregarious' is positive; 'antisocial' is negative — but a SOLITARY person is not necessarily antisocial.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Productive, making lots of work
Barren, producing little or nothing
Famous, well-known by many people
Brief, lasting a short time only

questions.explanation: PROLIFIC = producing in large quantities (offspring, books, work, ideas). 'Prolific writer' = writes many books. (From Latin 'proles' = offspring + 'facere' = make.) ANTONYM = BARREN, sterile, fruitless, unproductive. Synonyms of prolific: productive, fertile, fecund, profuse. Common SSC + banking word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Brave, willing to take risks
Timid, lacking courage to act
Honest, truthful in dealings
Wise, with sound good judgement

questions.explanation: AUDACIOUS = bold, daring, fearless; sometimes recklessly so. (From Latin 'audax' = bold.) Can be positive ('audacious goal') or slightly negative ('audacious lie' = brazen). ANTONYM = TIMID, cowardly, fearful, cautious, fainthearted. Synonyms: bold, daring, brave, intrepid, fearless, plucky, valiant.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Outdated, no longer in any use
Modern, currently used and popular
Ancient, very old in age and date
Unique, one of a special kind only

questions.explanation: OBSOLETE = no longer in use, outdated, replaced. 'Floppy disks are obsolete'. ANTONYM = MODERN, current, contemporary, up-to-date, latest, in vogue. Synonyms of obsolete: archaic, antiquated, outdated, defunct, passé, redundant. Note 'archaic' = very old, often deliberately retained in some contexts; 'obsolete' = simply no longer used.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'TURBULENT'?

options.option_text: full of chaotic and restless energy
marked by peaceful calm and stillness
prone to sudden violent outbursts
lacking any clear order or direction

questions.explanation: B is correct because TURBULENT means characterized by disorder and unrest; its antonym is TRANQUIL or SERENE — both captured by 'peaceful calm and stillness'. A is a synonym of turbulent. C and D also describe instability, not peace.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'FRUGAL'?

options.option_text: exceedingly careful with money spent
inclined to spend money freely and lavishly
marked by extreme poverty and scarcity
unable to afford basic necessities easily

questions.explanation: B is correct because FRUGAL means sparing and economical; its antonym is EXTRAVAGANT — spending freely and lavishly. A is a near-synonym. C and D relate to poverty, which is a cause of frugality, not its opposite.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'TACITURN'?

options.option_text: excessively timid and easily frightened
speaking freely and at great length
reserved in manner and choice of words
habitually using very few words in speech

questions.explanation: B is correct because TACITURN means habitually silent and uncommunicative; its antonym is GARRULOUS — speaking freely at length. C and D are synonyms of taciturn. A is a common trap: timid and taciturn both describe withdrawal, but timidity is about fear, not silence.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'BENEVOLENT'?

options.option_text: showing genuine goodwill and kindness
deeply devoted to helping charitable causes
wishing harm and evil upon others eagerly
indifferent to the pain of those around

questions.explanation: C is correct because BENEVOLENT means wishing well; its direct antonym is MALEVOLENT — actively wishing harm. A and B are synonyms. D (indifference) is a frequent distractor as it implies no kindness, but MALEVOLENT requires active ill-will, not mere indifference.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'LETHARGIC'?

options.option_text: displaying sluggish and drowsy behavior
showing keen alertness and brisk energy
prone to excessive sleep and deep fatigue
lacking in motivation and inner ambition

questions.explanation: B is correct because LETHARGIC means sluggish and lacking energy; its antonym is VIVACIOUS or SPRIGHTLY — alert and briskly energetic. A and C are synonyms. D confuses lethargy with low ambition; one can be unmotivated yet physically alert.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'SYCOPHANTIC'?

options.option_text: excessively flattering and servile in manner
bold and direct in expressing honest views
overly critical and harsh in all judgments
reluctant to voice personal opinions openly

questions.explanation: B is correct because SYCOPHANTIC means insincere and servile to gain favour; its antonym is FORTHRIGHT or CANDID — honest and direct. A is a synonym. D is tempting because sycophants avoid honest views, but 'reluctant to voice opinions' is itself a form of sycophantic evasion. C (harsh critic) overshoots — bluntness is not required, only honest directness.

questions.stem: Which option is the ANTONYM of 'RECONDITE'?

options.option_text: dealing with obscure and little-known topics
requiring deep scholarly knowledge to grasp
clear and easily understood by most people
confined to a narrow circle of experts only

questions.explanation: C is correct because RECONDITE means abstruse and known only to a few; its antonym is LUCID or ACCESSIBLE — plain and widely comprehensible. A, B, and D are all synonyms or near-synonyms. The hard part: B ('requiring deep knowledge') sounds different but still denotes inaccessibility — a classic test-setter trap for RECONDITE.
